title: Semi-Ordered Permutation Moves
description:
# Semi-Ordered Permutation Moves

You are given a permutation `nums` of the integers from `1` to `n`.

The permutation is called semi-ordered when value `1` is at the first position and value `n` is at the last position. In one move, you may swap two adjacent elements. Return the minimum number of moves needed to make `nums` semi-ordered.

## Example 1

**Input**
nums = [2,1,4,3]

**Output**
2

**Explanation**
Swap `2` and `1` to move `1` to the front, then swap `4` and `3` to move `4` to the end.

## Example 2

**Input**
nums = [2,4,1,3]

**Output**
3

**Explanation**
Value `1` starts to the right of value `4`, so their movement paths cross. The shared crossing means the direct counts overlap by one move.

## Constraints

* `2 <= nums.length == n <= 50`
* `nums` is a permutation of the integers from `1` to `n`.

solutions.name: Position Formula
solutions.description:
## Approach
Scan the array once to find the index of value `1` and the index of value `n`. Moving `1` to index `0` costs `posOne` adjacent swaps, and moving `n` to index `n - 1` costs `n - 1 - posN` adjacent swaps.

## Key Insight
If `1` starts to the right of `n`, the two values must cross each other. The direct sum counts that crossing twice, so subtract one in exactly that case.

## Complexity Analysis
The scan touches each element once, so the time complexity is O(n). Only two index variables and the answer are stored, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Simulate Adjacent Swaps
solutions.description:
## Approach
Actually perform the allowed operation. First bubble value `1` left until it reaches the first position, then find value `n` in the updated array and bubble it right until it reaches the last position.

## Key Insight
This route follows the operation definition directly. It is slower than the formula, but it makes the overlap case concrete because moving `1` can change where `n` is before the second phase begins.

## Complexity Analysis
In the worst case, bubbling can perform O(n) swaps and each swap is constant work, so this implementation runs in O(n^2) time under the stated small constraint. It modifies the input array in place and uses O(1) extra space.

solutions.name: Count Blocking Elements
solutions.description:
## Approach
Count how many elements are before value `1`, and count how many elements are after value `n`. These two counts are the blockers that must be crossed by adjacent swaps.

## Key Insight
A blocker immediately corresponds to one required adjacent swap. When `n` begins before `1`, one blocker relationship is shared by both targets, so the two blocker counts overlap by one.

## Complexity Analysis
The two directional scans are linear, so the time complexity is O(n). The algorithm stores only counters and positions, so the space complexity is O(1).
